ordered_diagnoses: Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) infection

s1.syndrome_frame: Acute febrile illness with multi-organ involvement and epidemic potential
salient_findings: Fever, headache, sore throat, and general discomfort
Leukocytosis, thrombocytopenia, and elevated liver enzymes
Bilateral pleural effusion, pericardial effusion, and liver edema
key_facts: 42-year-old male with no prior health problems
Living in an HFRS epidemic area
Not vaccinated
Developed symptoms six days before admission
Initial body temperature: 36.5°C
Pulse rate: 86 beats per minute
Respiratory rate: 18 beats per minute
Blood pressure: 118/77 mmHg
Slight flushing of the face
Leukocytosis present
Elevated lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) and alpha hydroxybutyrate dehydrogenase (α-HBDH)
Thrombocytopenia
Elevated urea, uric acid, and creatine levels
Declining levels of lymphocytes, CD8+ T cells, and NK cells
Positive serological test for HTNV immunoglobulin M (IgM) and IgG
Positive COVID-19 nasal and throat swabs

shortlist.why_kept: Positive serological test for HTNV immunoglobulin M (IgM) and IgG, living in an HFRS epidemic area

shortlist.label: Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) infection
shortlist.why_kept: Positive COVID-19 nasal and throat swabs, acute febrile illness

shortlist.label: Hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS)
shortlist.why_kept: Epidemic area, renal involvement, and hemorrhagic symptoms

shortlist.label: Leptospirosis

raw.rationale: Positive serological test for HTNV immunoglobulin M (IgM) and IgG, living in an HFRS epidemic area, and symptoms consistent with HFRS such as fever, headache, and thrombocytopenia

rejected.label: Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) infection
rejected.why: Although COVID-19 nasal and throat swabs are positive, the clinical presentation and laboratory findings are more consistent with Hantavirus infection

rejected.label: Hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS)
rejected.why: HFRS is a broader category that includes Hantavirus infection, but the specific diagnosis of Hantavirus infection is more precise given the positive serological tests

rejected.label: Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome
rejected.why: This condition presents with similar symptoms, but the positive serological tests for HTNV IgM and IgG point more specifically to Hantavirus infection

rejected.label: Leptospirosis
rejected.why: There is no clear evidence of exposure to water or soil contaminated with Leptospira, and the laboratory findings do not specifically support this diagnosis
